author: ribeye
dek: The national average is $4.36 a gallon — the first October it has ever topped $4 — and one Newark commuter has started budgeting like gas is a second mortgage.
disclaimer: Parody: the Mercer family of Newark is fictional. The record-high October gas prices are real, as reported by AAA in October 2026.
headline: Newark Family Does the Math on the Most Expensive October Gas Ever

ohio_story: NEWARK, Ohio — Tom Mercer filled up his truck on Church Street on Thursday morning, watched the total climb past $70, and did what any Licking County commuter would do: he stood there doing long division on his phone while the pump clicked. He drives to Columbus for work five days a week, down Route 16 and back, and at $4.36 a gallon nationally — the first October the average has ever topped $4 — the math has gotten personal.

"I used to just fill it up and not look," Tom said, tucking the receipt into his visor like it was a parking ticket. "Now I look. I look at the gallons, I look at the total, and then I sit in the truck for a minute and think about my life choices. My daughter asked if we could still go to the Wildcats game Friday night, and I said, 'Honey, the game is free. It's getting there that costs money.'" His wife, Carla, has responded the way Newark responds to everything: with a spreadsheet and a casserole. She has started packing his lunch, batch-cooking on Sundays, and routing all errands through a single loop past the Kroger on North 21st Street so nobody makes a separate trip for one forgotten onion.

The Mercers have not canceled anything yet, though the fall trip to Buckeye Lake has been downgraded from a weekend to a day trip, and Tom has begun referring to his truck as "the second mortgage." Carla's one concession to the moment is that she now lets him buy the good coffee at the gas station. "He's driving to Columbus and back on $4.36 gas," she said. "The man has earned a large dark roast."
real_summary: The average price of a gallon of regular gasoline in Nevada fell 4 cents in the past week to $5.45, AAA reported on Oct. 8, 2026, and the national average dropped 5 cents to $4.36. Even with the small declines, pump prices remained at record highs for autumn. "Gas prices remain the highest they've ever been for this time of year," said Doug Johnson, spokesperson for AAA Mountain West Group. "This is the first year the national average has been above $4 per gallon in October."

Crude oil was back above $90 a barrel after dipping into the $80 range for several days, AAA said, with volatility in the Strait of Hormuz continuing to pressure prices. Hurricane Isaias was another factor that could affect gas prices, AAA noted, if oil production and refineries in the Gulf region were impacted. The cheapest gasoline markets in the country included Indiana at $3.81 a gallon, while California topped the list at $6.40.

U.S. gasoline demand had eased, according to new Energy Information Administration data cited by AAA, falling from 8.84 million barrels per day to 8.68 million, while total domestic gasoline supply slipped from 206 million barrels to 204.4 million. West Texas Intermediate crude rose $1.04 at the close of Wednesday's trading session to settle at $90.42 a barrel.
source_note: AAA Mountain West Group release, Oct. 8, 2026: national average $4.36 a gallon, record highs for autumn, first October above $4.
